The meta, explained

Speed barely moves. Acceleration does.

Every stat becomes a level from 0 to 25. The game then looks that level up in a multiplier table. Some tables barely change from level 0 to 25. Others more than double. That spread, together with what the best players actually pick, is the meta.

How far each stat can move

Multiplier range across all 480 driver–vehicle pairings, road terrain. ×1.00 is neutral.

What the top 100 drove

Coins pay light builds first

The speed bonus from coins, by coins held. Every combo reaches the same +5% at 20 coins. Coin speed bends the curve, so it decides how soon you get there.

    1

    Light drivers rule online

    The four lightest characters share one stat class. It has the highest acceleration, mini-turbo, handling grip and coin speed in the game.

    2

    Coins pay light builds first

    Everyone gets the same bonus at 20 coins. Coin speed decides how early it arrives: at 5 coins the best combo already has +3.0%, the worst +0.6%.

    3

    Speed is three stats

    Road, off-road and water speed are separate stats. Baby Blooper is +2 on road but −3 off-road and on water.

      How the numbers work

      Level = driver points + vehicle points, clamped to 0–25 (main 0x515300). The game reads that level's multiplier from the performance table each frame (0x65b660). It also picks road, off-road or water speed and handling from the surface under the wheels. Blank table cells are ×1.000 (0x3e01f0, 0x1fc0b50). Standard Kart and Plushbuggy fall back to class V01 (0xab2dc0). CPU racers use a separate row, so these numbers are for players.

      Food isn't a stat. It's a timed boost and is left out.

      Sources

      Stats: from the game files. Competitive picks: Nintendo's Mario Kart World Open results. Vehicle renders: the game's highest-detail models and textures, path-traced in Blender Cycles at 3840×2560. Character art and fonts come from the game's UI.
